answer: Anchor each agent identity to one real-world credential proved in zero knowledge. A new agent shows a ZK proof that its government ID is valid and never used before, without revealing it. The network stores only a nullifier, so a second registration with the same document is instantly rejected. Forging an army of fakes means stealing or buying thousands of genuine IDs, a voyage no rational attacker undertakes: each identity costs money and legal risk, while a hollow pile of synthetic personas collapses on first check. Like onyx, it resists counterfeit, verifies easily.
